items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. The shipped close sentence reads 'just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.43.16 and no oshb:Isa.43.16, and no splice of that frame stands anywhere in the row; the only other close-side signal cited is the setumah after MT 43:15 (tier-3, single-witness), which cannot warrant a seam alone. The claim itself is byte-true: MT 43:16 is verse-initial כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.43.16, byte tier), a divine-owned frame; the contiguous-skeleton sweep on כה אמר (skeleton tier; count object: skeleton substring, verse count) returns 48 verses book-wide and exactly 4 in chs 41-43 -- MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16 -- so the auditor's digit holds and the 43:15|43:16 seam is sound. The web: keying does not evidence the frame either: WEB 43:16 reads “Yahweh, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters,” (web:Isa.43.16), the English 'says' falling only in the following verse, so the frame is verifiable solely in the MT bytes the row never splices. The row's sole tier-1 close warrant therefore ships outside the mandatory engagement class. Not high (nothing byte-false, no boundary defect); not low (this is the only close warrant, not ancillary disclosure). Medium confirmed; the proposed splice-with-tier repair is the right cure.

Re-derived both ways. The field as shipped is exactly as the auditor describes: rival plus a since-clause, no refusal. But the refusal ground the auditor supplies is already the row's own boundary argument: the row splices its onset frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.14, byte tier) and closes 'just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16', and device_notes states that the merged reading 'is disclosed above'. Bytes: MT 43:14 and MT 43:16 are both verse-initial frames -- כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, byte tier) -- both in the divine-frame class, with no frame inside MT 43:15 (the כה אמר skeleton is absent from that verse, skeleton tier), so two frames stand where the rival sees one complex; the rival's own since-clause ('both open on a Yahweh...says pattern') concedes as much. The rival is thus adjudicated by the row, in boundary_rationale rather than in the field, and the field contract (one sentence plus an optional mandated-rival sentence) does not require the refusal there. What remains is a disclosure shortfall: read alone, the field argues for the merge and points to no counter, and the second frame the refusal rests on is unspliced (that is item P12-003#1, not counted twice here). Not a defective warrant in substance, so not medium; not nothing, since the field records only the rival's case. Downgrade to low; the proposed one-clause refusal note is a fair minor repair.

Re-derived both ways. MT 44:1 in full is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier): no fear-not stands in it -- the pair skeleton אל תירא is absent from the verse at skeleton tier and no token carries the verb skeleton תירא (skeleton tier) -- and WEB 44:1 reads “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1). The formula stands one verse later, אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier); a byte-tier sweep of that exact pointed pair returns 4 verses (MT 37:6, 41:10, 43:1, 44:2; count object: pointed two-token form, verse count), so the auditor's 43:1 identity claim holds at byte tier. The named-servant half of the descriptor is byte-true at 44:1: יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier). The book-order neighbour row places the koh-amar frame and the fear-not it governs 'one verse inside the unit rather than at the onset', so the two rows do locate one formula at two verses. The seam survives without the misplaced formula: the adversative-plus-imperative onset וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier), whose first token matches MT 43:1's וְעַתָּ֞ה (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) at accent-stripped tier only; the verdict close at web:Isa.43.28; and the setumah after MT 43:28 (tier-3, single-witness, confirmed in the inventory). A seam warrant naming a formula at a verse that carries it in neither witness is a defective warrant, not alone load-bearing. Medium confirmed; the proposed relocation repair (onset signal at 44:1, fear-not cited at 44:2 with web:Isa.44.2 added to refs) is byte-sound.

Re-derived from the staged consonantal layer. The skeleton of וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) is ואתם עדי and the skeleton of וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier) is ועדיהם המה (both skeleton tier): distinct strings. The witness tokens alone, עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier), give skeletons עדי and ועדיהם (skeleton tier): distinct, and not identical at accent-stripped tier either; the only relation is that the shorter skeleton is a contiguous substring of the longer -- root sharing with containment. The row's label was tested charitably: a substring collate of the 44:8 token against the whole of MT 44:9 does return skeleton tier, which is presumably how 'matching at skeleton tier' arose, but the row asserts it of 'the two forms', and the two-token run collated against MT 44:9 returns none. The run's own convention treats the identical containment relation as non-identity: the neighbour rows call כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) against כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) 'not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier' although the shorter skeleton כי גאל is likewise contained in כי גאלתיך (skeleton tier). Under the tier-disclosure standard a recurrence claim's tier label is a byte-checkable claim, and this one overstates, inside a device_notes disclosure that is not load-bearing (the cut rests on the 44:8|44:9 participant shift, and the row discloses the pull rather than acting on it). Medium confirmed; the proposed relabel (root-level with containment; skeleton added to the non-identity list) is correct.

Re-derived both ways. The row's own splice וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) carries the rock token צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier), skeleton צור (skeleton tier). Tyre at the head of its oracle is מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier), whose name token has the two-consonant skeleton צר (skeleton tier), the same skeleton the adversary/narrow family carries. Neither shares the epithet's skeleton: the two-consonant skeleton is not a contiguous substring of the three-consonant one (nor the reverse), no token of MT 23:1 contains the rock skeleton, and no token of MT 44:8 contains the Tyre skeleton. The contiguous-skeleton sweep on צור (skeleton tier; count object: skeleton substring, verse count) returns 23 verses with no chapter-23 verse among them, and it does include the besieged and fortified forms נְצוּרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.8, byte tier) and מָצ֑וֹר (oshb:Isa.19.6, byte tier) the auditor names, alongside the plene rock sites MT 17:10, 26:4, 30:29 and 44:8; the sweep on צר (skeleton tier) is a different, pervasive object (133 verses, six of them in ch 23). So 'the adversary and Tyre homographs sharing its skeleton' is byte-false at the tier it names; the hazard catalogue's 'homograph triple' is a sweep-hazard grouping, not a skeleton identity. The digit prong is secondary (the clause is not a universal claim) and does not move severity. The clause is a disambiguation aside: the closing rock epithet is itself byte-true and the close seam rests on the 44:9 participant shift, so the false claim is not load-bearing. Medium confirmed; either proposed repair (drop the clause, or restate it against the classes that do share the skeleton, with a digit) is byte-sound, and the Tyre/adversary contrast survives only as a pointed-form contrast.

Re-derived from the mark inventory (MT keys, single witness): SAMEKH at MT 44:20, no mark at MT 44:21 or 44:22, PE at MT 44:23, no mark at MT 44:24, next SAMEKH at MT 44:28. The section that PE closes is therefore MT 44:21-44:23 and its end falls at 44:23|44:24 -- the row's own closing seam for span Isa.44.23-Isa.44.23, not the far side of it -- and that end separates 44:21-23 from the verse-initial frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier; a K/Q verse per the inventory, the splice standing clear of the K/Q pair) rather than grouping them with it. The layer's only pressure runs against the front seam 44:22|44:23, where no mark stands and the section carries across, which is exactly the row's disclosed rival. Both directional claims in the shipped sentence ('on the FAR side of the row's own closing seam'; 'grouping Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 with the koh-amar oracle that follows') are inverted, and the book-order neighbour row states the same PE correctly (section Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 grouping its span with the following doxology). The cut is unaffected: the row rests it on the addressee turn רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) and says the tier-3 layer does not drive it, and the redeemer catchword note stands as shipped. A defective tier-3 mark claim, not alone load-bearing. Medium confirmed; the proposed restatement (PE closing MT 44:21-44:23 at the row's closing seam, weak corroboration of that seam, pressure against the front seam) matches the bytes.

Re-derived both ways. MT 45:9 opens ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier) and MT 45:10 opens ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier): two verse-initial tokens of skeleton הוי (skeleton tier; sweep: 22 verses book-wide, count object: skeleton token, verse count; the only ch-45 sites are these two, both verse-initial), and both sit in the book's woe-oracle-onset class, so the disclosed split rival rests on a tier-1 onset signal at 45:10, which the row itself concedes ('each opens on its own hoy exclamation'). Mark inventory (MT keys, single witness): SAMEKH at MT 45:7, 45:8, 45:9 and 45:10, nothing at 45:11, PE at 45:13 -- the SAMEKH after 45:9 falls inside the row's span at exactly the rival's split point, leaving each woe its own section in that layer. The row lists all three marks in boundary_evidence_refs but its prose engages none of them, sets confidence high and frontier_flag_considered false, while the preceding book-order row meets the same shape (SAMEKH after MT 45:7 backing its isolate-45:8 rival) at medium with the flag set: the calibration is inconsistent within the run. The row's merge warrant is byte-true as far as it goes -- both woes stand between the verse-initial frames כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ (oshb:Isa.45.1, byte tier) and כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) -- and the merge is a legitimate reading under the hybrid granularity rule against per-woe fragmentation, so this is no boundary defect and no respan is warranted. But confidence is a warrant-level claim with governance consequences (band-driven sidecar and frontier handling), and 'high' against an acknowledged tier-1 rival signal plus an undisclosed internal section mark is a defective claim, not a merely mechanical one; the missing prose disclosure compounds it. Medium confirmed; the proposed disclosure in device_notes plus the step to medium with the flag set is the right cure.
